codes.note: LLM judges rated mental-health QA responses and were compared with expert ratings on the same clinically grounded dimensions.
ChatGPT, GPT-4 and Vicuna judged sentence relevance to BDI-II depression symptoms; compared with labels from three expert assessors, one a psychologist.
LLMs extract advance care planning information (code status, decision maker) from EHR notes; this is clinical information extraction, not coding of a psychological construct.
The main reference is self-reported PTSD scores, but human raters also scored the narratives, so LLM–human agreement may be reported.
An LLM judge and licensed clinicians used the same rubric to rate chatbot safety in suicide-risk conversations; agreement is reported (IRR 0.81).
LLMs vs human rater on fictional narrative craft features; mostly literary style, though explicit emotion labelling is borderline psychological.
GPT-4 zero-shot coded online posts for motives, norms and emotions; compared against trained human coders.
GPT-4o agreement with human labels is for disinformation vs trustworthy content, which is not a psychological construct; the emotion analysis is not compared with human coding.
Claim matching for misinformation fact-checking; not a psychological or clinical construct.
LLM scored Rorschach Morbid Content and was compared with human assessors (kappa .72-.74, ICC .94-.95).
LLM-judge rubrics for role-playing agent quality and user satisfaction are checked against human judgments, but these are not mental-health or clinical constructs.
Surgeons rated LLM answers about orthopaedic fractures; no LLM coding of the texts, and the topic is not psychological.
Gynecologists rated LLM answers about premature ovarian insufficiency; no LLM coding and no psychological construct.
Commentary letter on an LLM study extracting neuro-oncology treatment symptoms; not empirical, and the symptoms are not psychological.
LLM recommends medication for depression vignettes, compared with expert choices; this is treatment decision support, not coding a psychological construct in text.
Specialists rated how accurate ChatGPT's answers on vasectomy were. ChatGPT did not code or rate any text, and the construct is not psychological.
Inference-time LLM behaviour control method; no coding of psychological text against human raters.
This record is a PREreview (peer commentary). The original LLM-judge vs clinician safety-rating paper is eligible and should be screened separately.
GPT-5 scored CLASS on classroom transcripts and was compared with human raters. Teacher-child interaction (emotional support) is educational but possibly interpersonal-psychological.
AI voice-to-text for medical affairs documentation; no LLM coding of psychological constructs compared against human coders.
LLMs pulled oncology treatment-discontinuation reasons (progression, intolerance, death) from clinical notes; this is not a psychological construct.
GPT-3 applies an expert codebook to curiosity-driven questions (cognitive behaviour); agreement with expert coders is reported.
LLMs (ICL and instruction fine-tuning) identify MI client change/sustain talk; results are likely measured against human-annotated MI codes.
ChatGPT coded emotions and FACS action units from facial photographs, compared with a FACS specialist. The material is images, not text.
LLMs apply MISC codes to real MI counselling transcripts, and their codes are compared with expert annotations in a bilingual English–Dutch dataset.
LLM generative agents simulate urban travel behaviour; no coding of psychological text against human coders.
GPT-4/Llama-2 run PTSD assessments from transcripts of clinician-administered interviews; clinicians rated the same interviews, so the reference is human ratings.
Humans annotate emotional support quality of LLM and fan responses; the abstract mentions no LLM rating the same responses.
Dermatologists rated chatbot answers about herpes zoster. No LLM did any rating, and the topic is not psychological.
Microtubule image segmentation using vision foundation models; no psychological text and no LLM coding.
The LLM relevance classifier was validated against human coders. It's unclear whether the entitativity and emotion coding was done by the LLM and checked against humans.
Narrative review of AI in breast care (senology); not psychological text, and no LLM–human coding agreement.
LLM extracts immune-related adverse events of immunotherapy from oncology clinical notes; this is medical adverse-event coding, not a psychological construct.
An LLM extracts reporting and open-science practices from published articles. That is metascientific data extraction, not coding of psychological text.
LLMs identify early maladaptive schema labels in mental-health forum posts; the reference labels are likely human annotations, to be confirmed in full text.
Surgeons rated ChatGPT/Gemini answers on clavicle fracture management; orthopedic, not psychological, and no LLM coding task.
Claude coded the evaluative stance toward AI in medical journal abstracts; this is stance coding of scientific literature, not a psychological construct.
LLMs rate C-SSRS suicide severity of Reddit posts, compared against human annotations.
GPT models and trained research assistants coded the same goal and essay texts for spirituality, and the abstract reports how well their scores agreed.
GPT-4 coded wisdom-related constructs in conflict narratives; compared with expert human coders, reporting kappa and agreement.
Fine-tuned Llama-2 scores open-ended question complexity on a creative question-asking task; correlates with human ratings (r = .84).
LLMs coded patient narratives, validated against clinician coding; domains include psychological burden, but the construct is mostly medical patient experience.
Multimodal LLM labels emotion against human MELD labels, but the input is mainly video and speech, so it is unclear whether text is coded.
LLM and human annotators both gave emotion labels to lexicon words; unclear whether LLM–human agreement is reported, and the units are words rather than texts.
ChatGPT coded forum posts for behaviour-change mechanisms; extraction precision compared with human coding. Kappas may be mostly LLM–LLM, so needs checking.
Generic sentiment classification of IMDB movie reviews; no psychological or clinical construct in the text.
Biomedical information extraction (NER and relation extraction) from PubMed abstracts on the gut-brain axis; this is not psychological text coding.
Philosophical essay on ChatGPT and human judgement; no empirical LLM coding or comparison with human raters.
GPT-3.5/4 and MedAlpaca classify wellness dimensions in mental-health text and are evaluated against expert-labeled datasets (MultiWD, WellXplain).
Human raters scored the quality (EQIP) of LLM-generated bipolar information; no LLM rated the same texts.
Qwen3 only creates soft labels to augment training data for an encoder-based recognizer; its labels aren't checked for agreement with human annotations.
ChatGPT is the subject of the tweets, not a coder; sentiment is classified with lexicon tools and classical ML (SVM).
Anesthesiologists rated LLM-generated patient-education answers; no LLM coding of psychological text against human labels.
Med-PaLM 2 estimated depression/PTSD scores from patient interviews and compared them with human clinical raters' scores.
Surgeons rated LLM answers to spine FAQs for accuracy; no LLM coding of texts and the topic isn't psychological.
ChatGPT-4o/4.5 and human coders coded open-ended responses about ACEs and mentoring; the codings were compared in SPSS, so agreement is likely reported.
New annotated datasets of Chinese social-media posts (suicide risk, cognitive distortions); eight LLMs evaluated against the labels, which are presumably human annotations.
An LLM judge rated chatbot suicide-risk safety in conversations using the same rubric as licensed clinicians; reports judge-clinician agreement (IRR = 0.81).
Fine-tuned Bio_ClinicalBERT (an encoder model) detecting venous thromboembolism in oncology notes; not a psychological construct and not a generative LLM.
Humans rated chatbot answers about HPV vaccination for accuracy and quality. This is not a psychological construct, and no LLM coded or rated text.
GPT-4o, Claude, and Gemini rated 39 distress items from Korean psycho-oncology interview transcripts; agreement with psycho-oncologist ratings was ICC 0.816–0.872.
This is about oncology decision support: oncologists rated LLM treatment plans, and no psychological construct was coded.
Surgeons rate how well LLM trauma-surgery recommendations follow guidelines; the topic isn't psychological and no LLM does any coding.
An LLM judges the safety of responses in mental-health crisis dialogues, and its judgments are checked for agreement with expert assessments.
An LLM identified psychotherapy dissatisfaction in forum posts, and human raters validated its outputs, so agreement figures are likely in the full text.
Correspondence/commentary on LLM medical diagnosis accuracy; not empirical and not a psychological-text coding task.
LLMs map emotional expressions onto Reversal Theory families and four raters do blind coding; unclear whether LLM–human agreement is reported.
LLMs undergo affect induction; only human raters score the LLM's sentence completions, and no LLM codes the same texts against humans.
Editorial on ChatGPT in scholarly writing; no LLM coding of psychological text and no comparison with human coders.
LLM codebook annotations, including emotion, compared with two human coders on depression videos, but the data are video keyframes rather than text.
LLM classification of financial sentiment and brand involvement in news, compared with human labels; no psychological or clinical construct.
LLM rates therapeutic alliance in text-based counseling conversations; expert evaluations on a subset using the same framework serve as the reference.
LLMs triage cybersecurity vulnerabilities using the SSVC framework; the texts are not psychological or clinical.
Gemma and trained raters (DDCI) both coded dream affect in the same narratives; unclear whether same scheme or whether LLM–human agreement is reported.
GPT rated the hedonic valence (affective dynamics) of narratives and was compared with human ratings of the same texts. The correlation is reported.
LLMs rate occupations (not psychological texts) on RIASEC/Big Five; validated against crosswalked O*NET benchmarks, not human coding of the same texts.
Benchmark of MLLMs rating therapist Facilitative Interpersonal Skills in psychotherapy responses against expert human ratings; text modality likely included.
Misinformation emotion/stance study using deep-learning classifiers; generative AI only used for synthetic data generation, not LLM coding versus humans.
LLMs detect mental manipulation (an interpersonal construct) in dialogues; evaluated against the human-annotated MentalManip dataset labels.
ChatGPT and Claude coded interpersonal emotion regulation strategies in narratives; kappa reported against human coders.
Benchmark of emotional inference in scenarios labeled by trained annotators and designed for evaluating LLMs; LLM–human comparison likely in full text.
LLM generates marketing narratives that humans and automated text analysis then rate; the LLM does no coding checked against human coders.
GPT-4 Turbo/fine-tuned LLMs labeled psychiatric symptoms in interview transcript segments; evaluated against mental health expert labels (accuracy, F1).
Social-media posts on drug use and overdose were annotated by LLMs and humans together; LLM–human annotation agreement may be in the full text.
Human qualitative metaphor analysis of students' views of GenAI; no LLM codes or rates any text.
Physicians rated the outputs of LLMs on PET/CT tasks. No LLM did any coding against humans, and the construct isn't psychological.
Zero-shot LLMs label emotions in conversation utterances and are evaluated against human benchmark labels plus a re-annotation by four human annotators.
LLM-assisted interrater reliability on coding self-reported health outcomes; mostly physical, though the 35 aspects may include mood or mental health.
LLM agent infers emotions in text on emotional reasoning benchmarks; unclear whether the reference labels come from human annotators.
LLM-as-judge pipelines rate psychosocial risk (psychological harm, manipulation) of responses, compared with human safety annotations in PKU-SafeRLHF.
LLM classifies cognitive distortions in patient utterances; F1 computed against a public, likely human-annotated dataset.
Fine-tuned LLMs scored open-ended AIHQ hostility and aggression responses, and their scores were compared with trained human raters.
Audio LLMs judge the speaking style of generated speech (pace, pitch, emotional expression); this is not psychological or clinical text coding.
ChatGPT-based detection of cognitive distortions in patient speech, likely evaluated against human-annotated distortion labels.
Specialists and patients rated LLM answers for NMOSD patient education; no LLM rated anything, and the topic is not a psychological construct.
Qualitative literature review on AI and posthuman teaching; no LLM coding of psychological text against human coders.
LLM rated fidelity of lay-provider mental health sessions on 6 domains; ICC/AC2 agreement with human supervisor ratings reported.
LLAMA3 deductively coded psychosocial autopsy interviews about suicide; Cohen's kappa agreement with qualitative researchers was reported.
Main task predicts crisis-counseling outcome (criterion), but LLM-generated features may be compared with human-annotated domain knowledge.
Peer review of a statistics methods paper on binary judgments; no LLMs and no coding of text.
LLM sorted EHR terms into mental-health categories and was compared with clinician consensus (κ reported); this is borderline between psychopathology coding and medical term coding.
Human raters scored chatbot answers about TBI and concussion. No LLM rated the same outputs, and the questions are medical information, not psychological text.
Patient queries were annotated for empathy applicability by both humans and GPT-4o, and the abstract reports human–GPT alignment.
